environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 2000 m (6562 ft)
environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent noncondensing; 5 to 93 percent short term
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F) normal operation
environmental.storage-temp: -40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.optics-qsfp: 40 GbE QSFP+, QSFP+ direct attach and active optical cable, breakout cables to SFP+
features.optics-sfp-plus: 10 GbE SFP+, 1 GbE and 100 Mbps SFP, SFP+ direct attach cable and active optical cable
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 switches in a ring; also a Virtual Chassis Fabric leaf or spine and a QFabric node

management.oob: management port C0 (RJ-45, em0) and C1 (SFP, em1) with link and status lamps
management.usb: one USB port for image updates

performance.qsfp-plus-speeds: 40 GbE; or four 10 GbE with a breakout cable
performance.sfp-plus-speeds: 10 GbE with SFP+ optics; 1 GbE or 100 Mbps with SFP optics

physical.weight-note: 21.8 lb (9.8 kg per the guide, 9.9 kg per the datasheet) with FRUs installed (Table 3)

power.power-input-ac: 110 to 240 VAC single phase (datasheet); the guide's table gives no value
power.power-input-dc: rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating range -40 to -72 VDC, 10 A maximum (guide Table 17)
power.redundancy-note: two supplies, load-sharing and fully redundant; both should be installed

thermal.fans: five fan modules, hot-swappable; the switch runs 30 seconds without thermal shutdown while one is replaced

configs.description: QFX5100-48S-3AFO: the 48S-AFO with the three-port management panel (a second SFP port, C0, above C1). The supplies and fan modules are those of the AFO build.

gaps.wanted: The datasheet prints 150 W for the QFX5100-48S-AFO/AFI under "Power Consumption", the guide 230 W typical and 365 W maximum for the 48S and 48SH (Table 14). Same device, no measure or scope stated for the 150 W. The guide's figures are carried.
The datasheet gives -36 to -72 V DC; the guide's Table 17 gives -40 through -72 VDC (rated -48 to -60). The guide's range is carried.
The guide's Table 14 prints no value for AC input voltage, line frequency or current in the PDF held. The datasheet gives 110-240 V single phase; the chassis label in the photograph reads 100-240 V.
The part number of the four-post mounting kit, and its depth ranges. The guide describes the kit and flush or recessed mounting in prose and a figure per chassis but gives no part number.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port "for image updates" and gives no generation. It is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.
The vertical rating label at the right edge of the rear (an AC input line and a DC input line). It is only partly legible in the photograph and is not drawn.
The yellow laser-safety triangle at the lower right of the port side. It is a label, not a feature of the metal, and is not drawn.

The 48S photograph shows no fan numerals, fan icons or supply symbols on the strips beside the slots, where the 48T photograph shows them. The guide numbers the fan slots 0 to 4 and its figure draws the marks. They are not drawn on this device.

A photograph or flat drawing of the three-port management panel on a 48S. The guide's figure 22 draws it (the right-hand panel: a stacked pair of SFP cages, then console, C0 and USB) without scale, and the only photograph of it is the 48T's. The rear-3mgmt view takes the 48T photograph's arrangement and positions, and the model chip reads QFX5100-48S, which is an assumption for the 48SH, whose chip text is not shown anywhere held.
The datasheet's ordering table lists QFX5100-48S-D-3AFI and -D-3AFO (DC supplies, three management ports); the guide's Table 1 lists no such 48S model. They are not modelled.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

chassis.note: guide Table 3: 1.72 in (4.3 cm) high, 17.36 in (44.1 cm) wide, 20.48 in (52 cm) deep, 21.8 lb (9.8 kg) with FRUs. The datasheet gives 4.37 x 44.09 x 52.02 cm and 21.8 lb (9.9 kg); the two weights are one figure rounded two ways (21.8 lb is 9.89 kg), so 9.9 is carried. The width is the body: the mounting brackets are not part of it and are not modelled.

colour.note: The front plate around the ports samples #727580 (5 by 5 px means at two bare patches) and the rear panel #80858b. The photograph is lit warmly and these are its values, not a paint reference.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide says the switch mounts flush or recessed 2 in (5 cm) in a four-post rack with the mounting kit shipped with it (a pair of front rails and two rear blades; twelve screws), and gives no part number for the kit; the datasheet says only "versatile four post mounting options". The library holds no kit contract for it and none is written here, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 440.9 mm chassis, without brackets.

gate-1.note: The front studio photograph is orthographic enough to measure. Its body is 1442 px wide and 143.5 px high (top edge row 43, bottom row 186.5), an aspect of 10.05 against the table's 440.9 / 43.7 = 10.09, 0.4 percent out. Scale 3.270 px/mm across and 3.284 down. The rear photograph reads 1457 x 143.3, an aspect of 10.17 (0.8 percent out), at 3.305 px/mm across and 3.28 down. The guide's flat figure 14 is a 761 x 135 px thumbnail and is used to count and to read the printing only.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. The guide and the datasheet (July 2024) state none. Reseller trackers (router-switch.com) list announcements of 2020 to 2022 for the QFX5100-24Q, -24Q-AA and -96S part numbers and none for the 48S, so the device states none announced. Estimated, because the trackers are not the maker.

mgmt.note: The 48S photograph shows the two-port panel of Table 1 (QFX5100-48S-AFO, -AFI, -DC-AFO and -DC-AFI have two management ports): C1 is the SFP cage (em1) and C0 the lower of the two stacked RJ-45 jacks (em0); the upper jack is the console. The status and link lamps of C0 sit in the lower corners of its jack. The guide's figure 22 also draws a three-port panel (a second SFP cage, C0, above C1), which Table 1 gives the -3AFO and -3AFI models and the 48SH. That panel is the `rear-3mgmt` view. Its arrangement is read off the 48T photograph, which has the same three-port panel, because no 48S photograph of it is held.

modules.note: The fan modules (QFX5100-FAN-AFO and -AFI) and the 650 W power supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AFO, -AFI, and the DC -AFO and -AFI named by the datasheet) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. The guide says to fit a blank cover over an empty supply slot but names no part number for it, so no blank is modelled and no empty-bay configuration is offered.

port-lamps.note: Two dots flank each SFP+ numeral, 5.86 mm apart, centred on the cage; the guide's Table 8 and figure g050235 name them the Link/Activity lamp (left) and the Status lamp (right), and Table 9 gives their states. Four dots stand at 4.07 mm pitch beside each QSFP+ cage, above the upper cages and below the lower ones (Table 10, figure g050236, bi-colour). The photograph resolves all of them (the numerals beside them resolve at the same scale), so none is carried from the drawing alone. The first lamp of a QSFP+ port is the link lamp of an unchannelized port; the other three are channel lamps (Table 10).

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off the photograph and figure 14: the SFP+ ports run 0 to 47, even above the upper row and odd below the lower row, the numeral between its two lamps; the QSFP+ ports are 48 and 49 down the first column, 50 and 51, 52 and 53, the numeral at the left of each cage. Interface names are not printed on the unit. The guide's examples use xe-0/0/n for the 10 GbE ports and the Junos names of the QSFP+ ports are not given in the guide held; none is written to the manifest.

ports.note: Front photograph. The lamp dots above the upper row give each cage centre: 24 columns on a pitch of 46.5 px, 14.22 mm, which is the registry's 14.25 SFP+ ganged pitch, in four groups of six columns. The first cage centres are at 17.28, 106.05, 194.8 and 283.5 mm, a group stride of 88.77 mm, so the gutter is 88.77 - 6 x 14.25 = 3.27 mm; the cells start at 10.15 mm. Then six QSFP+ cages in three columns on a pitch of 62 to 62.5 px, 18.96 to 19.1 mm (the registry's 19.0 is used), the first cage face from 377.2 mm. Counts are 48 and 6, the guide's callouts 2 and 3 of figure 14. The cells use the registry's apertures (14.25 x 10.4 and 18.5 x 9.58); the photographed cage faces are larger (about 11.8 mm and 12.7 mm high) because they include the bezel.

power.note: guide Table 14 (AC): typical 230 W, maximum 365 W for the 48S and 48SH; Table 17 (DC): typical 300 W and maximum 385 W for the 48S, 48T and 24Q. The datasheet's "Power Consumption" prints 150 W for the 48S-AFO/AFI without a measure or a scope. 150 W is below the guide's typical 230 W under the same unqualified reading, so the two disagree and are recorded as a gap, not reconciled. The guide's figures are filed as the device's.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph, read at 3.5 times and checked against the guide's figures 20 and 22 (the figure 20 drawing is lettered EX4600-40F: a drawing of a sibling, used for the arrangement only). At the left a 63.5 mm panel carries the four chassis lamps ALM, SYS, MST and ID, the C1 SFP cage with two lamps above it, the console and C0 jacks stacked in one shield, the USB port and the reset pinhole. Then five fan slots on a 48.95 mm pitch, each preceded by a strip with a small dark status lamp, then two supply slots on a 61.1 mm pitch, and at the right edge a dark strip carrying a vertical rating label. The fan and supply slots measure 41.5 x 41.3 mm and 54.8 x 39.8 mm.

rear-photo-vs-drawing.note: The guide's figure 20 draws the rear of an EX4600-40F; the studio photograph is the real QFX5100-48S and wins. The photograph is the back-to-front (AFI) build with blue fan handles lettered AIR IN (AFI) and blue supply handles lettered AFI. The default configuration here is front-to-back (AFO) with Juniper Gold handles per Tables 13 and 19; the AFI configuration matches the photograph.

row-pitch.note: Down the first SFP+ column the cage faces run from 75.0 to 113.5 and 117.5 to 155.5 px, centres 94.3 and 136.5 px, which is 15.6 and 28.5 mm below the top edge, a row pitch of 12.9 mm. The QSFP+ cage faces centre 14.4 and 29.4 mm below the top edge, a row pitch of 15.0 mm. The registry's 15.0 SFP row pitch is measured on a different cage and is not a conformance figure, so the photograph's 12.9 is used; the 10.4 mm cell fits it. y is good to about 0.3 mm.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5100 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2023-02-26, 254 pages (Juniper Networks; terms: the guide's own copyright notice and the Juniper EULA, a reference copy kept outside the repository): Tables 1 (models), 3 (physical specifications), 8 to 12 (lamps), 13 and 14 and 16 (AC supplies), 17 and 18 (DC supplies), 19 to 21 (fan modules); figures 14 and 15 (port panels), 20 to 25 (management panel), 26 to 40 (supplies, fans and airflow). QFX5100 Ethernet Switch Datasheet, 1000480-022-EN, July 2024: the ordering table (variants, the DC supplies, the fan modules), weight and dimensions, power. Juniper's studio photographs of the 48S, front and rear, 1500 x 256 and 1500 x 228 px (image library, qfx5100-48s-front-high and -rear-high), and of the 48T. The held-sources folders of the intake area were not readable from this worker (permission denied), so no Visio stencil or 3D model could be looked for there; none is named by the guide or the datasheet either.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the latch tongue at the foot of every upper cage and at the top of every lower one, so both lips face the band between the rows: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention. The QSFP+ pairs show the same.

vents.note: Two staggered rows of hexagonal holes along the top edge (0.2 to 4.6 mm) and one band along the bottom (39.5 to 43.5 mm), and a vertical strip of hexagons, 9.0 mm wide, between the SFP+ and QSFP+ blocks. They are drawn as vent strips; the hexagon pitch (about 4.4 mm along the strip) is read off the photograph at 3.5 times and is estimated, as the pattern is a rectangular approximation of a staggered hexagon field.
